rationale:
Evidence from iteration 0 (score 256): the oval finishes 40% of the time, but the s-bend and slalom both end by leaving the track, at mean progress 0.32 and 0.12. Their max_error (0.063 and 0.062) is above the 0.06 m off-track limit, and line-loss events are 1.55 and 2.0 per run. The sensor spread of +/-0.02 m is narrower than the excursions these bends cause, so the robot loses the tape and then reacquires it late. Steering oscillation is about 0.27, which points to too little damping. Body width cannot help: the off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), and the 0.06 floor binds across the whole body range, so I am leaving body_width alone.

Changes: (1) Widen the sensor array to x = -0.03 to +0.03 m in 15 mm steps, and enlarge sensors to 16 mm so adjacent footprints overlap. This keeps tape visible at lateral errors up to about 0.04 m and should cut line-loss events. (2) Raise kd from 0.4 to 0.8 to damp the jitter from sensor lag. (3) Lower base_speed from 1.6 to 1.5. This is a small trade: it adds a little time, but it reduces the lateral slip and lag on the sharp s-bend and slalom sections, where the robot currently leaves the track. The oval already finishes at 1.9 s, so there is some time margin. Expected result: fewer off-track exits on the s-bend and slalom, a higher mean progress, and lower line-loss counts. Oval completion should hold. Hypotheses to test: (a) the wider array removes most line-loss events; (b) kd 0.8 cuts steering_oscillation below 0.2; (c) finish time stays under 3 s on the oval.
